content.comment_body: So, I understand that input I8 only supports a 0-10 volt signal and cannot directly accept milliampere current signals, correct?
That's correct. However, you can convert a 0/4-20 mA current signal to a 0/2-10 V voltage signal by placing a 500 Ω resistor in the circuit.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion clarified that input I8 on the [product_name] module only works with voltage signals (0-10V), not direct current (mA). One participant confirmed this and offered a solution by using a resistor to convert a current signal to a voltage input. This reveals that users may sometimes be uncertain about which input types are supported by [product_name] modules.
